newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian siege man tied to girlfriend's skull.
newsitem.headline: Australian siege man tied to girlfriend's skull.

text.p: A lovesick Australian has tied himself to a traction rope supporting his girlfriend's skull in a bizarre hospital siege which has lasted two days, Perth police said on Wednesday.
Doctors fear any sudden movement by the unarmed man could ruin the woman's chances of recovering from spinal injuries sustained in a car crash and risk leaving her paralysed.
Ivan Garvan, 31, on Monday used his jumper to tie himself to the halo traction rope which supports a metal ring screwed into his 29-year-old girlfriend's skull, police said.
The traction equipment holds the unidentified woman's head still, immobilising her damaged spinal column.
Garvan has not slept nor had any food or water since the siege began on Monday in the spinal ward of the Royal Perth Rehabilitation Hospital in Western Australia state.
"It appears to be a relationship gone wrong and he just wants to be with her," Perth police superintendent David Parkinson told reporters on Wednesday.
"This without doubt would be the most unusual incident that this police service has ever encountered," Parkinson said.
